title: At 15, Uma Kashvi Becomes Youngest Player Ever Signed in WPL Auction
excerpt: Delhi Capitals bought the Karnataka all-rounder for Rs 10 lakh in Kochi — 15 years and 202 days old, with an Under-15 average of 172 behind her.
body:
• Delhi Capitals signed Karnataka all-rounder Uma Kashvi for Rs 10 lakh at the WPL 2027 mini-auction in Kochi, at her base price with no competing bids.
  • At 15 years and 202 days, she is the youngest player ever to secure a Women's Premier League contract, breaking the record set by Deeya Yadav, signed by Delhi at 16 in the 2026 auction.
  • Kashvi, a right-handed batter and right-arm off-spinner born on April 9, 2011, scored 516 runs at an average of 172 in the BCCI Women's Under-15 tournament, with three centuries.
  • She has already played for India Under-19 against Sri Lanka Under-19, taking four wickets in three T20Is and two more in two ODIs.

A 15-year-old from Karnataka is now the youngest player in Women's Premier League history. Delhi Capitals signed all-rounder Uma Kashvi for Rs 10 lakh at the WPL 2027 mini-auction at the Grand Hyatt in Kochi on Wednesday, securing her at base price in the uncapped all-rounder category with no competing bids. At 15 years and 202 days, she passes Deeya Yadav, whom Delhi also signed, at 16, in the 2026 auction. Two other 15-year-olds, Anshu Nagar and Avanya Jain, were in this auction but went unsold.

The record behind the signing

Kashvi's age-group numbers explain why scouts were watching. In the BCCI Women's Under-15 One-Day Trophy in 2025-26 she scored 516 runs at an average of 172, including three centuries and a half-century, and an unbeaten 158 off 66 balls against Manipur on January 10, 2026. She began cricket at seven, captained Karnataka at Under-15 level, and at 12 scored an unbeaten 217 in a Bengaluru inter-school tournament. She is part of Karnataka's Under-19 team, has won the Under-19 T20 Trophy and the Karnataka Women's League title, and stepped up to India Under-19 this year for the series against Sri Lanka Under-19.

"She's been on our radar for a little while. Our scouts have watched her play extensively and shared some incredible feedback, and I've seen her play as well. We believe she could become an absolute superstar in the future."

— Jonathan Batty, Head Coach, Delhi Capitals

Delhi's auction in full

Delhi spent Rs 1.05 crore at the auction to complete a 17-member squad, on top of 13 retained players and Rs 13.9 crore in retention spending, for a total squad cost of Rs 14.95 crore. Their marquee buy was Kiran Navgire for Rs 75 lakh; Kashvi, Nazma Khan and Scotland spinner Kirstie Gordon joined for Rs 10 lakh each. Head coach Jonathan Batty called Navgire probably the most dynamic and powerful batter in the auction, and described the Kashvi signing as a long-term investment. Reporting of Delhi's auction is at MyKhel.

The auction around her

A total of 146 players — 119 Indian and 27 overseas — competed for 27 slots across the five franchises, and about 25 players were signed, 14 of them uncapped. UP Warriorz, who entered with the largest purse of Rs 3.75 crore, made the auction's biggest buy, Australian all-rounder Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 crore, and also added Grace Harris, Sneh Rana and Sushma Verma. The fifth WPL season runs from January 14 to February 7, 2027. Full squad lists are at TeluguNow's auction roundup.

What a contract at 15 does and does not mean

A WPL contract at 15 is a development bet, not a guarantee of playing time. Kashvi joins a squad with established Indian and overseas internationals, and her first season is more likely to be measured in training exposure and occasional opportunities than in a regular place in the XI. The comparison being drawn in Indian coverage is with Vaibhav Suryavanshi's impact in the men's IPL — but the honest reading of Delhi's own comments is patience: the franchise scouted her extensively, paid base price, and framed the signing around what she could become. Her Under-19 international experience at 15, and an Under-15 average of 172, are the concrete evidence that the bet is grounded in performance rather than novelty.
